name: Poppy purple
lede: Poppy purple is a near-black, warm neutral that ColorHub's library carries as the English gloss of Messhi, a Japanese traditional color name.

sections.title: A dark neutral by way of Japan
sections.body:
ColorHub's library records this hue only through a Japanese entry: *Messhi* (滅紫), glossed in our data as "Poppy purple" [1]. The kanji reads, more literally, toward a faded or spent purple, and our sources carry no separate Western record, Ridgway plate or ISCC-NBS block for the name, so an English coinage date is undocumented here [1]. At lightness 22, chroma 9, Poppy purple sits so dark and so low in chroma that it reads as a brown-black rather than a true purple on screen [2].

The nearest named color is [[dante|Dante]], 3.2 units away and marginally warmer; [[veinous-blood-red|Veinous Blood Red]] sits 3.3 units off, close enough to be mistaken for the same swatch [2]. [[graphite|Graphite]], a cooler, less reddish near-black, is 5.3 units away, and [[zulu|Zulu]] is 5.5 units off [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Poppy purple in 292 of 23,781 paintings, 1.23 percent, as photographed, more common than 71 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It most often sits as a shadow, in 36 percent of its paintings, and peaks in the 1900s, in 26 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.4 times the expected rate [3]. The earliest match is dated 1414, in a panel by Lorenzo Monaco, with no single painter standing out above the rest of the archive, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. As with any near-black, the measured hex is a screen approximation of a varnished, aged photograph, not a pigment identification [3].
